newsitem.title: USA: MFRI sees 20 pct rise in FY97 revenues.
newsitem.headline: MFRI sees 20 pct rise in FY97 revenues.

text.p: MFRI Inc, which makes industrial filtration products, said Friday it expects revenues for the fiscal year ending January 31, 1998, to rise 20 percent to $115 million.

According to a statement, David Unger, chairman, said at the annual meeting that results for the fiscal second quarter appear to be tracking the company's internal projections based on measurements such as new bookings, intake margins and productivity.

"We are particularly pleased with the first quarter performance and the prospects of our Perma-Pipe and Thermal Care businesses," Unger said. "The outlook for Midwesco Filter has improved, based on an increase in bookings in the second quarter and the strengthening of both sales and margins for filtration products."
Unger added that contemplated changes in U.S. environmental regulations may increase demand for Midwesco's filter bags in the future.
"Midwesco is serving an international market for bags and bag related products and services that is estimated to reach $630 million in 1997," Unger said.
He added that MFRI's volume and margins were rising, positioning the company for profitable long-term growth.
"Our objective is for earnings per share to increase at a faster pace than revenue growth, and we believe the strategies are in place to achieve that goal," Unger said.
